title: per-org-route-circuit-breaker-silent-slowdown
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Summary: We observed a class of incidents where per-org circuit-breaker and per-route quota policies interact to cause silent slowdowns (requests permitted but throttled to micro-delay loops) and undercounted billing. This ticket tracks investigation, a reliable repro, root cause, and a safe rollout for fixes.

Observed behavior: During a regional failover + policy rollout window, some customers see a persistent ~20-200ms added latency on requests to affected routes and simultaneously have usage undercounted in billing metrics by ~5-15% for the window. No explicit 429s are emitted; traffic is allowed but slowed. Errors are not increased.

Why this matters: Latency surprises break SLAs and customer UX; undercounted usage leads to billing discrepancies and reconciliation burden. The pattern affects per-org heavy clients using route aliases + burst credits.

Repro steps (dev environment):
1) Start local enforcer with the following two policy objects loaded: per-org circuit breaker (threshold 95th p95 CPU=0.8 for 30s) and per-route burst allowance (burst=1000 tokens).
2) Configure route aliasing: route A -> canonical route C with per-route override throttles.
3) Send sustained parallel requests (RPS 500) with a token that has per-org burst credits applied.
4) Initiate a policy rollout that changes the circuit-breaker TTL (simulate remote policy update) while simultaneously rotating the route alias mapping.
5) Observe enforcement logs: decision path shows a stale policy pointer for some requests, and a late-path fallback triggers the internal backoff code path which performs short sleep loops before allowing tokens to proceed.
6) Check billing exporter: aggregated counters are updated only on full-request-completion code path; requests that exit via micro-delay loop do not always increment per-route meters due to early fast-path permits.

Evidence:
- snippet from enforcer logs (anonymized):
  [2025-02-28T14:03:12.312Z] enforcer:decision id=abc123 route=A applyPolicy=v1 -> allowed fast-path
  [2025-02-28T14:03:12.332Z] enforcer:decision id=abc124 route=A applyPolicy=v0 -> fallback delay-loop sleep(20ms) -> allowed (no meter increment)
- billing exporter logs show gap between decision timestamps and meter increments matching the delay window.
- metrics: enforcer.decision_latency_p99 increases by ~150ms for affected orgs; billing.meter_emitted_count drops by ~7% over the same window.

Hypothesis / Root cause: Race between policy cache invalidation and per-request enforcement pointer update. When a request is routed to an execution shard that has a stale pointer to the old per-org policy version, the enforcer executes a fallback codepath (legacy circuit-breaker soft-fail) that introduces internal micro-sleeps instead of performing canonical token-burn/meter emit. The code path was intended to throttle aggressively with explicit 429s, but an earlier refactor changed the fallback to allow-through with delay to preserve UX. Because meter emission logic was moved to the canonical path post-refactor, requests that took the fallback path were not reliably incrementing per-route/per-org meters.

Immediate mitigations taken:
- Rolled back the policy rollout and pinning on regional edge nodes (Mar 1 02:00 UTC).
- Temporary alert created: enforcer.decision_vs_meter_delta > 3% for 10m triggers PagerDuty.

Proposed fixes (priority order):
1) Short term (safe, quick): Ensure fallback path performs meter increment prior to delay loop. Minimal code change with targeted unit tests.
2) Medium term: Replace pointer-style policy access with versioned immutable policy objects and atomic swap. Requests should always reference an immutable policy instance so there is no partial-update window. This requires runtime changes to policy cache + GC.
3) Long term: Centralize billing emission to the request admission layer (before enforcement fallback) so meters are emitted on admission decision, and moves billing emission to an idempotent, side-effect-safe emitter that tolerates retries.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for fallback path to assert meter increments and exported counters match allowed request counts.
- Integration test that simulates concurrent policy rollout and route alias changes. Reproduce the 7% undercount in CI with controlled timers.
- Load test in staging with synthetic org that mirrors heavy-client characteristics (bursty tokens, route aliasing).

Rollout plan:
- Merge short-term fix behind a feature flag (enforcer.fallback_emit_meter=true). Canary to 5% edge nodes for 24h and watch enforcer.decision_vs_meter_delta, latency p99, and 429 rate.
- If stable, increase to 25% for 6h, then full rollout.
- Medium-term versioned policy change scheduled after short-term is stable; perform canary deploy with read-only policy snapshots and GC window of 1h.

Monitoring & Alerts:
- New metric: enforcer.fallback_path_count and enforcer.fallback_meter_mismatch_count.
- Update dashboard for enforcer.decision_latency_p99 and billing.meter_emitted_count per-org per-route.
- PagerDuty runbook added for escalation and manual rollback steps.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Do we accept a small window where fallback path emits meters twice under extreme retry cases? Prefer idempotency at emitter level vs guarding fallback emission with dedupe token.
- Memory & GC impact of keeping immutable policy objects around longer to avoid races. Need SRE input on memory budgets per shard.

Dependencies: ["ENG-30109", "ENG-421007"]

Stakeholders: ["Lena Fischer (SRE)", "Diego Morales (Billing)", "PM: Nina Roberts"]

Acceptance criteria:
- No undercount >1% in staging during synthetic rollout test.
- Canary shows decision_vs_meter_delta within historical baseline for 24h.
- Unit + integration tests land and pass in CI.
- Runbook updated and oncall notified.

Links / artifacts: ["https://github.com/redwood-inference/enforcer/pull/7281", "https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/ENF-rolling-policy-cache-design", "dashboard:enforcer/policy_cache_mismatch"],

Next steps:
- (Arjun) implement short-term fix and open PR (target: 2025-03-05).
- (Maya) prepare staging load job and monitor dashboards during 5% canary.
- (Lena) provide guidance on memory budget for versioned policy retention window.
comments: 2025-02-28 - Arjun: Initial report from SRE after noticing billing delta and latency bump during routine regional failover. Created ticket and attached anonymized logs.
2025-03-01 - Maya: Deployed a temporary pin to stop ongoing rollouts in the region; opened short-term rollback for edge nodes. Observed immediate drop in decision_latency_p99 back to baseline.
2025-03-03 - Diego: Billing team confirmed a 6.8% undercount for affected orgs in reconciliation batch. Agreed this is high-priority to fix before monthly invoicing.
2025-03-04 - Arjun: Drafted quick fix patch that emits meter on fallback path and added unit tests. Preparing PR.
